text:
Maya: Reworked the runtime edge-case handling for prefix/KV cache eviction — addressed the comments from yesterday's review. PTAL when you have a moment; I added a focused unit test and a small smoke script.

Jamal: Thanks Maya! Can you summarize the behavioral change? I skimmed but want to make sure we're not changing LRU semantics.

Maya: Short summary:
- Avoid removing active KV entries during async flushes by gating on inflight refcount
- Added a fallback path that returns cached prefix if eviction would block generation
- Moved allocation->rotation ordering to prevent transient double-free in error path

Code snippet I added to clarify the check:
```
if (kv_entry->inflight_refs > 0) {
  // keep it, schedule background compaction
  continue;
}
```

Elia: Nice, that addresses my concern about stalling the streaming path. PTAL at the tests though — one assertion seemed flaky locally.

Maya: Good catch — flaky assert was due to timing in the smoke harness. I switched to an event wait and added retry logic. Updated test: `tests/runtime/test_kvcache_eviction.py::test_inflight_preserve`.

Ciara: PTAL @Jamal @Elia — this is ready-ish for a final pass. If we can get two approvals today I can schedule a canary slot tomorrow morning.

Jamal: Will review in the next hour. If green I'll +1 but requesting Elia for a second approve due to the allocator change.

Elia: Scanned and ran tests locally. LGTM aside from one nit in the comment, added inline suggestion. :+1:

Maya: Thanks! Addressed the nit and pushed a tiny README note about the smoke script usage.

deploy-bot: Canary slot requested for maya/runtime-kvcache-eviction at 2024-11-12T09:00Z — queued

Maya: Re-requesting review (PTAL) — I've squashed the test fix into the main commit and added the smoke script to `ci/smoke/runtime_kvcache.sh`. Hoping to grab that canary slot. :crossed_fingers:

Jamal: Reviewed and approved. :white_check_mark:

Elia: Approved after nit applied. Go ahead with canary.

Maya: Thanks all — will kick the canary and report back with perf/latency delta. Thread closed unless something pops up.
